# Case 3 — Same-context cold critique fixture

Input is **provided textual copy and a provided visual description**, not a supplied image: "Never worry about money again. Guaranteed! 97% of customers agree." Described: gradient, five fonts, three CTAs, tiny brand. No visual was actually inspected and no real campaign outcomes were observed.

**Supplied observable details:** unsupported numerical "97%" and absolute "Guaranteed!" wording; described five-font hierarchy and competing CTAs.

**Subjective opinion:** message is overpromising, crowded, lacking a recognizable emotional truth. Brand likely too small for useful recall — a hypothesis, not measured recall.

**Subjective 5D:** clarity 2, surprise 1, emotion 2, recognition 1, visual 1 (provisional as image not seen) = **7/25, Rebuild**. **Review provenance:** internal same-context critique, not blind, not audience evidence.

**First fix:** remove unverified "guaranteed" and "97%" and clarify the actual proven service. Rewrites: "Your books. One less thing to carry." / "Less bookkeeping. More doing." / "For the days you already have enough on your plate." Test which one communicates an accounting service before publication.

**Evidence needed:** actual image, substantiated product capabilities, and real cold-reader reactions.
